step_roles_retired: WP-3.1: a step no longer carries a role. The closer was something a reader worked out from roles and order, which made the last step written the closer; a need now declares closing_authority. step_roles is kept because plan gold v3, v3.1 and v3.2 are frozen in the shape that uses it, and a superseded dataset must keep a vocabulary that defines its tokens. No code reads it.
effect_ownership: WP-3: what acting on a capability does to the world outside this system is REGISTRY metadata, declared once per capability ('effect' above), and is not a property of a planned step. Measured reason: in the 201-call shadow the planner wrote BOUNDED_WORKFLOW 38 times against EXTERNAL_STATE_CHANGE 4, while all 7 procedure steps of the frozen gold say EXTERNAL_STATE_CHANGE and nothing downstream separated the two. BOUNDED_WORKFLOW has no declaring capability in v3.0 and AuthorityVocabularyContractTest pins that count at zero.
procedure_rule: PROCEDURE only for an external state change or a bounded business workflow; when reading entity state resolves the request, the plan ends at ENTITY_STATE (product-owner decision 2026-09-20). Upheld in WP-3 by the capability's own declared effect plus PROCEDURE_WITHOUT_ORDER_PRECONDITION; in WP-3.1 the same rule is PROCEDURE_WITHOUT_ORDER_READ — a procedure resolution must REQUIRE the ENTITY.ORDER read, which is an absence rule rather than a position rule.
closing_rule: WP-3.1: a need DECLARES the single authority that resolves it (closing_authority). The plan must require at least one capability of that authority; several capabilities of the SAME authority may resolve it together, which the frozen gold does 4 times. Step order is execution order and carries no closing meaning — reordering a need's steps cannot change what resolves it. A fallback to the seller is not an authority: it is a resolution outcome (NEEDS_SELLER / CAPABILITY_GAP) the runtime records after the plan has run. Superseded: the WP-3 rule, where exactly one authority CLOSED and a genuine multi-authority need was written PRECONDITION then CLOSES.
sequence_rule: WP-3: step order is the dependency. The explicit depends_on index left the wire — it was used on exactly the 7 procedure steps of the gold and every one pointed at the ENTITY.ORDER read the registry already requires, so it carried no information a reader did not have. WP-3.1: order still means execution order and nothing else; it no longer identifies the closer.

customer_goal.adopted: Inquiry v3.5, 2026-09-20 — the Resolution Planner is EXPERIMENTAL / NOT_ADOPTED_FOR_PRODUCTION and the vocabulary below replaces it as the only thing an LLM produces in this path.
customer_goal.vocabulary_verdict: four requested_outcome values, measured not assumed. v1: all 72 frozen resolution goals map, 60 settle without judgment, 12 ambiguous about WHICH of the four, ZERO need a fifth value and ZERO are unmappable. v2 (classes A/B/C adjudicated by the product owner 2026-09-20): 68 goals emitted, 1 ruled NO_GOAL, 3 still open (D/E/F). Still zero new values.
customer_goal.procedure_rule: only an ACTION may reach a procedure. A DECISION asks to be told a judgment and does not authorise a side effect, which is the C6 defect stated as a structure rather than as a sentence in a prompt.
customer_goal.decision_rule: a DECISION goes to KNOWLEDGE first — the decision RULE is knowledge — and reaches SELLER only from an OBSERVED absence. AUDITED 2026-09-20 against the frozen gold: 3 of 5 DECISION goals require observed ENTITY_STATE before a judgment can be produced (S:T7a and S:T7b carry ENTITY.LISTING in the gold itself; S:T12a carries ENTITY.ORDER). The dispatch table is unchanged — the rule declares its own prerequisites — but the loop must be able to RESUME the resolver that named one. See resume_rule.
customer_goal.substitution_rule: capability availability never changes a goal. A resolver that COULD NOT RUN settles at CAPABILITY_GAP with the registry's reason; a resolver that RAN AND FOUND NOTHING settles at NEEDS_SELLER. Reporting a seller judgment for an unreadable source would be asserting that no policy exists.
customer_goal.no_new_terminal_states: the loop's end states are the existing resolution_states above, unchanged. Of the seven candidates the brief offered, six already existed and the seventh ('the system can go acquire this') is already gap_reasons.ACQUIRABLE. ACTION_REQUIRES_APPROVAL was deliberately NOT created: every procedure here is DECLARED_NO_EXECUTOR, so it has no producer, and approval belongs to the execution lane that already owns it.

entity_state_requirement.rule: a required DIMENSION is satisfied by any one of its fields; a goal is answerable when every required dimension is satisfied. Optional fields are recorded when readable and are never fatal.
entity_state_requirement.why: all-or-nothing made a harmless over-read fatal (P01, C4); field-level let a spare readable field hide a genuinely missing one (R:7a8136b2). Required dimensions pass both, and 'any readable field resolves it' stays refused.

customer_goal.resume_rule: a resolver that named a prerequisite is WAITING, and the prerequisite's result is not the goal's answer. When the prerequisite has run and the waiter has not been heard from since, the waiter is re-dispatched. Without this the loop settled on whatever the prerequisite returned: measured, a DECISION whose policy needed the order's fulfilment state reported RESOLVED having evaluated no decision. A GAPPED prerequisite still ends the goal and is checked before the resume. Nothing looks ahead: the prerequisite was named by a resolver AFTER running.
customer_goal.no_goal: a message may carry no customer resolution goal. That is NOT 'ignore' — the case still exists and may raise VOC / complaint / issue signals elsewhere. The Layer-A scorer treats a NO_GOAL row as unassignable, so any goal emitted on one is invented by definition.

new_in_v3.SCOPE_MOVES: same closing authority, different instance — the frozen step reads something the adjudicated referent is not about
new_in_v3.GOAL_SPLITS: one frozen row, two customer goals

legacy_gold_conflicts.rule: declared, never suppressed, and deliberately NOT re-derived: re-labelling the frozen resolution gold is a separate decision with its own evidence rows.

goal_relations.what_it_is: a relationship between two goals of ONE message that the CUSTOMER stated: 'send just the nozzle; if that is impossible, refund me.' One row of the frozen 72 carries one.
goal_relations.stated_condition: MANDATORY and the customer's own words. Without the clause there is no evidence a relationship was stated, so two goals from a message with no conditional clause CANNOT be related — blank is refused by the constructor and by the wire schema.
goal_relations.why_it_is_not_a_planner: one kind, and it is a thing customers say. There is no SEQUENCE, no DEPENDS_ON, no THEN and no PREREQUISITE, so an execution order between goals is not expressible. It relates GOALS and never capabilities, authorities, steps or gap reasons. ResolutionPolicy has no parameter that could carry one.
goal_relations.shape: a forest of chains: at most one fallback per goal, at most one incoming per goal, no cycles. Never a graph.

fallback_activation.activates_on: NOTHING. There is no producer in this runtime of the fact the condition needs.
fallback_activation.the_line: CAPABILITY_GAP is NOT semantic impossibility. It says what THIS DEPLOYMENT could not attempt and says nothing about what the seller will do. Every procedure in this registry is DECLARED_NO_EXECUTOR, so every ACTION goal ends at CAPABILITY_GAP — a runtime reading a gap as a refusal would refund every customer who ever wrote a conditional sentence.
also_not_a_refusal: NEEDS_SELLER — nobody has written down whether it is possible, which is the opposite of knowing
RESOLVED / RESOLVED_CONDITIONAL — an answer was produced
fallback_activation.runtime_disposition: WITHHELD_FOR_CUSTOMER_STATED_CONDITION — no resolver is asked for the goal at all, and it is handed to the seller with the clause attached.

waiter_resume_state_machine.A: a resolver that names a prerequisite is WAITING
waiter_resume_state_machine.B: when the prerequisite produces an observation, the waiter is dispatched again
waiter_resume_state_machine.C: when the prerequisite gaps, fails, finds nothing or asks the customer something, the waiter is NOT resumed and the goal settles in the prerequisite OWN state
waiter_resume_state_machine.D: a prerequisite succeeding is never the goal being resolved
waiter_resume_state_machine.E: the same prerequisite cannot be asked for twice
waiter_resume_state_machine.F: a cycle R1 -> R2 -> R1 ends closed, detected by the same observation that catches a duplicate
waiter_resume_state_machine.G: bounded by MAX_WAIT_DEPTH = CapabilityId.values().length - 1 — the registry size, derived and not chosen, because a chain visits distinct capabilities
waiter_resume_state_machine.H: the resolver resumed is the EXACT capability that asked, not another of the same authority
waiter_resume_state_machine.I: the prerequisite's observation, with its provenance, stays in the trace for the resumed resolver to read

decision_resolver.not: 'knowledge, and the seller if there is none' — measured insufficient: 3 of the 5 DECISION goals in the frozen gold require observed entity state, and 2 of those carried the entity read in the gold before any re-adjudication.
decision_resolver.is: a DECISION resolver looks for the RULE that decides this goal. Knowledge is asked first because a rule is a thing the seller wrote down. Having found the rule, the resolver may find that applying it needs a fact and names THAT ONE capability as a prerequisite; the fact is read, the rule is resumed, and the decision is produced or is found to need the seller.
decision_resolver.who_decides_the_prerequisite: the resolver, after running. Never the Customer Goal Interpreter, which sees no capability at all.

prompt.payload_floor: the customer's message and two facts (surface, listing_resolved). Narrower than the planner's four: a goal never names an option and never asks for anything, so the option count and the askable inputs left the wire.
prompt.availability: NOT in the payload. Told what this deployment can do, a model rewrites what the customer asked for.

customer_goal.gold: eval-store:inquiry-customer-goal/v3 — 72 goals, 1 NO_GOAL row, 1 multi-goal row, 1 explicit FALLBACK, 0 open.

execution.status: EXECUTION_INFRA_FROZEN (2026-09-21) — the harness is finished and does not change again until a real smoke has produced results.
execution.command: cd backend && SELLEROPS_INQUIRY_GOAL_API_KEY=… SELLEROPS_INQUIRY_GOAL_ENDPOINT=… ./gradlew --no-daemon -q --offline runGoalSmoke --args='--approval <manifest> --granted-approval apr-… --granted-run <run-id> --out <dir>'
execution.one_command_covers: environment read · manifest load · frozen input assembly · every bound field recomputed from the world · GoalRunGuard.refusals · credential and output-collision checks · transport · raw streaming · derived rows · scoring · run-put · run-verify · report. Nothing is left for the operator to run afterwards.
execution.classpath: the TEST runtime classpath. The interpreter has no production caller and a task pointed at a main-tree entrypoint would quietly make that untrue.
execution.transport_is_bound: The live approval contract §4 already says the execution TOOL is part of the manifest, so `transport` is a bound field and a rehearsal approval refuses a vendor — in both directions, by the same comparison that refuses a moved commit. Without it a rehearsal manifest is a real manifest with a note on it.
execution.transport_default: REAL. Only the exact token FAKE selects the fake; unset, blank and misspelled all mean REAL.
execution.fake_cannot_reach_a_network: its endpoint is the constant fake://goal-smoke-rehearsal/no-network and it throws if handed any other; the real endpoint variable is not read in that mode.
execution.mode_is_read_off_the_object: GoalTransport.modeOf(transport) — a field claiming 'this is a real run' can disagree with the thing doing the sending, and the disagreement would favour the rehearsal.
execution.run_state: RUN_STARTED.json is written on the first row, after every check that could refuse — that instant is CONSUMED. RUN_COMPLETE.json is written only when the send loop returned and every observation is durable; its ABSENCE is what makes an interrupted run distinguishable from a finished one. A refused run leaves the directory empty.
execution.raw_is_primary_truth: finalization steps only ADD files; none writes raw.jsonl or rows.jsonl, none deletes, and a failing step is recorded and carried rather than thrown. The credential is REMOVED from the finalizer's subprocess environment — neither the scorer nor the store has any use for it.
execution.http_auth_failure_semantics: A — one request per input, so a bad credential records one HTTP_401 row per input and fourteen sends, not one send and a stop. This is ApprovalManifest.NO_RETRY's written contract ('one request per input; a failed call is a recorded failure') and is now pinned by a test. Short-circuiting on a fatal auth failure is PRODUCT_DECISION_NEEDED: a rejected request is not billed, so the cost is time rather than money, and stopping early leaves a corpus incomplete in a way nothing distinguishes from a crash.
execution.rehearsal_proof: GoalSmokeRehearsalTest starts the launcher in a separate JVM with a CLEARED environment: 14 fake sends, ordered rows, score/run-put/run-verify ok, no form of the credential anywhere. Six negatives (no credential · wrong identity · moved corpus · output collision · dirty tree then moved commit · killed after 5 of 14) all reach 0 sends or leave partial raw durable. Network 0 throughout.

planner_status: EXPERIMENTAL / NOT_ADOPTED_FOR_PRODUCTION (2026-09-20). step_roles, step_roles_retired, closing_authorities, closing_rule, sequence_rule and procedure_rule above describe the Resolution Planner contract, which is KEPT as a comparison and replay asset so the WP-1..WP-3.2 evidence stays readable, and which has never had a production caller. The authority vocabulary itself — authorities, capabilities, entity_fields, resolution_states, gap_reasons, customer_inputs, scopes, effects — is NOT deprecated: it is carried into inquiry-goal/v1 unchanged and is what customer_goal above is built on.
